newsitem.title: USA: ShopKo sees new strategy within weeks.
newsitem.headline: ShopKo sees new strategy within weeks.

text.p: - Retailer ShopKo Inc. said on Thursday it hopes to set a new corporate plan within several weeks following Wednesday's collapse of its $1 billion merger agreement with Phar-Mor Inc.
"It's a matter of weeks. We have done a lot of the preliminary work previously," chief executive officer Dale Kramer told investors in a telephone conference call.
Company executives also indicated that the new plan would likely focus on the general merchandise sector rather than the drugstore business as proposed in the defunct Phar-Mor deal.
"We believe that we have clearly demonstrated that this concept we currently have developed clearly works and our preference at this point would be to find similar businesses," he said.
Wall Street had disliked the Phar-Mor deal, contending that the companies were dissimilar and could not achieve sizable cost-savings. Phar-Mor is a drugstore chain.

ShopKo and Phar-Mor jointly called off the deal on Wednesday, citing unspecified uncertainties. Sources familiar with the companies cited a decline in Phar-Mor's stock price, regulatory delays and uncertainty about the position of one large Phar-Mor shareholder.
ShopKo management now will revisit a strategic plan that had been developed last spring by financial adviser Salomon Brothers before the Phar-Mor deal was announced.
"We've had no contact with other companies at this point. We'll continue to re-run the models we ran last spring and take a look at where the opportunities are," Kramer said.

ShopKo officials stressed that one of their major goals is to provide an exit stategy for major shareholder Supervalu Inc., which has publicly announced its intent to divest its position. Supervalu bought ShopKo in 1971 and then sold 54 percent of its stock in a 1991 public offering.
"I think we have a lot of options. The key will be creating the right exit strategy for Supervalu and leaving ourselves in a position where we could make some strategic acquisitions," Kramer said.
Shares of ShopKo rose 1/4 to 16-3/4 in afternoon trading.
ShopKo also said in the conference call that it sees acquisition opportunities to build on its growing ProVantage healthcare unit.
